_meta.purpose: Installation evidence catalogue · Agent A · pre-install + fixing topics (16 topics)
_meta.governance_rule: Evidence only. Zero installation procedures authored. 'expert_author_required' where source pool runs dry.
_meta.source_reuse_note: Reuses verified sources from data/nex-reference-brains/staircase-preparation/source_catalogue.json (src-001, src-009, src-016, src-017, src-021, src-025). New sources introduced this session for installation-specific evidence: src-INST-01 (BWF Timber Stair Installation Guide 2018), src-INST-02 (BWF pre-2018 v3 2015 withdrawn edition), src-INST-03 (NHBC Standards Chapter 6.6 Staircases), src-INST-04 (HSE INDG143 Manual Handling), src-INST-05 (HSE INDG401 Work at Height brief guide), src-INST-06 (HSE L153 CDM 2015 Managing health and safety in construction), src-INST-07 (Peter Brett Carpentry & Joinery textbook series).

new_sources_introduced.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018 current edition)
new_sources_introduced.document_title: Installation Guide — Timber Stairs: A Guide to Safe Stair Installation
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: Publication confirmed via BWF Stair Scheme news article (April 2018 launch) and NBS Publication Index. Direct PDF returned HTTP 500 on WebFetch this session but URL is BWF's canonical hosting and appears in multiple third-party mirrors (Stairbox, HBF, GD Woodworking, JELD-WEN).

new_sources_introduced.source_name: BWF Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2015 v3, withdrawn — mirrored by JELD-WEN + Stairbox)
new_sources_introduced.publisher: British Woodworking Federation / mirrored by JELD-WEN (UK) Ltd and StairBox
new_sources_introduced.publication_date: 2015 (marked 'Withdrawn' by NBS in favour of 2018 edition)
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: URL retrievable (1.1MB PDF) but binary body could not be parsed by WebFetch. Mirror is a JELD-WEN-branded version of the BWF Stair Scheme installation guide. Use 2018 current edition (src-INST-01) in preference; mirror kept for cross-reference.

new_sources_introduced.publication_date: Annual editions; NHBC Standards 2026 edition applies to homes with foundations begun on or after 1 January 2026
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: Chapter 6.6 subsection structure confirmed via New Build Inspections knowledgebase (6.6.1–6.6.17). Subsections 6.6.12 (Timber staircases), 6.6.15 (Proprietary units), 6.6.16 (Protection during construction) are the installation-relevant subsections. Note: NEX source_catalogue.json had NHBC referenced as 'Chapter 6' generally — this session confirms Chapter 6.6 specifically.

new_sources_introduced.source_name: HSE INDG143 — Manual Handling at Work: A Brief Guide
new_sources_introduced.document_title: INDG143 (rev4): Manual handling at work — a brief guide, referencing Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992 (MHOR)
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: Verified via HSE.gov.uk. Companion detailed document is L23 (Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992 — Guidance on Regulations).

new_sources_introduced.source_name: HSE INDG401 — The Work at Height Regulations 2005: A Brief Guide
new_sources_introduced.document_title: INDG401: The Work at Height Regulations 2005 — A Brief Guide
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: Verified via HSE.gov.uk landing page. WAHR 2005 (SI 2005/735) is the underlying statutory instrument. Relevant to stair install where operatives use temporary platforms above the stair void.

new_sources_introduced.source_name: HSE L153 — Managing Health and Safety in Construction (CDM 2015)
new_sources_introduced.document_title: L153: Managing health and safety in construction — Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015, Guidance on Regulations
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: Verified via HSE.gov.uk. CDM 2015 came into force 6 April 2015. Relevant to installation project coordination, principal contractor duties, RAMS for stair delivery/installation.

new_sources_introduced.source_name: Peter Brett — Carpentry and Joinery textbook series (Job Knowledge & Site Practice)
new_sources_introduced.document_title: Carpentry and Joinery — Book One: Job Knowledge (3rd ed, 1408506505) and Carpentry and Joinery for Advanced Craft Students: Site Practice
new_sources_introduced.publication_date: Multiple editions from 1990s through 2011 (3rd ed of Book One)
new_sources_introduced.verification_note: Long-standing UK Level 2/3 carpentry apprentice textbook aligned to CGLI 585 syllabus and City & Guilds 6706. Covers stair installation, setting out, plumb, level, wedges within the site carpentry curriculum. Specific chapter/page mapping not verified this session.

evidence.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018)
evidence.document_title: Installation Guide — Timber Stairs: A Guide to Safe Stair Installation
evidence.section_or_clause: Section 'Before installation' (BWF Stair Scheme confirms guide covers 'before installation' checks)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide contains a 'before installation' section addressing site readiness before a timber staircase arrives on-site, including protection of the stair from moisture from drying plaster/screed and confirming site conditions.

evidence.source_name: NHBC Standards — Chapter 6.6 Staircases
evidence.section_or_clause: 6.6.2 Design and Specification Information; 6.6.16 Protection During Construction
evidence.what_source_discusses: Subsections addressing pre-install specification/information handover and protection of the installed stair during subsequent construction trades on site.

evidence.source_name: HSE L153 — CDM 2015 Guidance
evidence.document_title: L153: Managing health and safety in construction (CDM 2015)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Framework for pre-construction information exchange and site coordination applicable to stair delivery/installation project planning.

evidence.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018)
evidence.document_title: Installation Guide — Timber Stairs: A Guide to Safe Stair Installation
evidence.section_or_clause: Section 'Checking delivery' (BWF confirms guide covers 'checking delivery')
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide contains a dedicated 'checking delivery' section covering receipt of stair components on site.

evidence.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018)
evidence.document_title: Installation Guide — Timber Stairs: A Guide to Safe Stair Installation
evidence.section_or_clause: Section 'Storage' (BWF confirms guide covers 'storage' of stair components before installation)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide contains a 'storage' section covering on-site storage of the stair before it is installed, with reference to moisture protection from drying plaster/screed.

evidence.source_name: NHBC Standards — Chapter 6.6 Staircases
evidence.what_source_discusses: Subsection addressing protection of stair components on site (relevant both to protection of stored components pre-install and installed stair post-install).

evidence.source_name: HSE INDG143 — Manual Handling at Work: A Brief Guide
evidence.document_title: INDG143 (rev4): Manual handling at work — a brief guide
evidence.section_or_clause: Whole document; risk filters for lifting/lowering/carrying/pushing/pulling; MHOR 1992 regulations
evidence.what_source_discusses: Statutory brief guide covering employer duties under Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992 applicable to any lifting/carrying task, including large joinery items such as staircase assemblies.

evidence.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018)
evidence.document_title: Installation Guide — Timber Stairs: A Guide to Safe Stair Installation
evidence.section_or_clause: Cross-referenced under 'working at height' / handling of stair components
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide references safe handling of stair components as part of the wider installation safety context.

evidence.source_name: HSE INDG143 — Manual Handling at Work: A Brief Guide
evidence.section_or_clause: Risk filters for lifting and lowering; simple filter for handling while seated
evidence.what_source_discusses: Provides the statutory framework and risk filter approach for lifting operations under MHOR 1992.

evidence.source_name: HSE — L24 Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992 ACOP
evidence.document_title: L24 Workplace health, safety and welfare — ACOP
evidence.what_source_discusses: Companion workplace safety ACOP — applicable when the stair-install workplace is itself a construction site (interacts with CDM 2015).

lifting.gap_note: No stair-specific 'lifting equipment' guidance found in web sources searched. LOLER 1998 (Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations) applies where mechanical lifting is used but no stair-installation-specific ACOP was located. Installation module authors should consult LOLER if manufacturer specifies mechanical lifting for pre-assembled flights.

evidence.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide contains a 'clearances' section which is the closest equivalent to route/access planning for the stair from delivery point to install location.

evidence.source_name: HSE L153 — CDM 2015 Guidance
evidence.document_title: L153: Managing health and safety in construction (CDM 2015)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Framework guidance placing responsibility on principal contractor for site access arrangements.

access_planning.gap_note: No dedicated public technical publication was found for 'route from delivery point to installation location' specific to timber staircases. This is largely site-craft judgement addressed within BWF's 'clearances' framing and CDM 2015 site coordination duties. If Installation module requires more detail, mark as 'expert_author_required'.

evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide covers assembly of the stair on site, which in installation practice includes the first-placement/dry-fit step.

evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide contains a dedicated 'temporary fixing of stairs' section covering bracing/propping arrangements before permanent fixings are made.

evidence.section_or_clause: Section 'Fixings and assembly' (BWF confirms guide covers 'fastening methods')
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide covers fixing methods for stair components including bottom-of-stair connections.

structural_interfaces.gap_note: For non-timber substructure (structural steel or masonry trimmer opening) additional consultation with the structural engineer / manufacturer's installation instructions is standard practice — this is a design-and-engineer interface rather than a stair-install topic.

evidence.source_name: BWF Stair Scheme Installation Guide — Timber Stairs (2018)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Guide covers alignment considerations within assembly and clearances sections though not as a named standalone section.

evidence.source_name: Peter Brett — Carpentry and Joinery textbook series
evidence.document_title: Carpentry and Joinery — Job Knowledge + Site Practice volumes
evidence.what_source_discusses: UK apprentice-level textbook covering site carpentry principles including alignment, plumb and level as fundamental setting-out disciplines.

alignment.gap_note: Alignment is a site-craft discipline embedded across BWF assembly guidance and City & Guilds training rather than a discrete standalone publication topic.

evidence.source_name: Peter Brett — Carpentry and Joinery textbook series
evidence.document_title: Carpentry and Joinery — Job Knowledge + Site Practice volumes
evidence.what_source_discusses: Standard UK carpentry apprentice textbook covering plumb verification as a fundamental setting-out principle applicable to newels and strings.

evidence.source_name: City & Guilds Level 2/3 Diploma in Site Carpentry / Bench Joinery (6706)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Qualification specification includes stair install units where plumb verification of newels/strings is an assessed competency.

plumb.gap_note: Plumb verification is not published as a standalone technical topic in stair guidance — it is embedded in general site-carpentry training. Installation module authoring should cite City & Guilds 6706 units and Brett's textbook rather than seek a stair-specific standard.

evidence.source_name: Peter Brett — Carpentry and Joinery textbook series
evidence.document_title: Carpentry and Joinery — Job Knowledge + Site Practice volumes
evidence.what_source_discusses: Textbook covers level verification of treads and landings as a fundamental site-carpentry discipline within stair construction.

evidence.source_name: Approved Document K — Protection from falling, collision and impact

evidence.what_source_discusses: Statutory guidance sets rise/going geometry which the installed stair must meet — indirectly requires level verification of installed treads.

evidence.source_name: City & Guilds Level 2/3 Diploma in Site Carpentry (6706)
evidence.what_source_discusses: Level verification of installed stair components is an assessed competency within stair install units.

level.gap_note: As with plumb, level verification is embedded in general carpentry training rather than published as a standalone stair-specific technical topic.
